title: CES contract registry
description: Which CES output-stream contract shards exist, what corpus each was recorded against, and whether that corpus has moved since. One scope per machine domain and per configured test-environment corpus. Generated by scripts/build-ces-contract-registry.py from the corpus and from the shards the recorder wrote; it records no engine behaviour of its own. The shards themselves are derived from 3-of-3 runtime agreement by RealityEngine_CI/scripts/regression-ces-contracts.py and live in that repo, because this repo owns the corpus and not the runtimes.

fingerprint.description: The corpus as a set of files and their content hashes. Per-file rather than a single roll-up, so a stale shard can name the machines that arrived, changed or left instead of only reporting that the count moved — incremental addition is the expected way this corpus grows.

members.description: relFile (as spelled in domains/corpus-index.json) to sha256 of the file's bytes. Bytes, not parsed content: deciding which JSON differences are semantically inert is a judgement this layer has no standing to make.

kind.description: domain — a directory under machines/domains/. corpus — a configured selection in RealityEngine_CI/config/*-corpus.txt, cross-domain by construction.

artifact.description: Where the shard lives, relative to this repo. Mostly ../RealityEngine_CI/..., which is the honest shape: the corpus is here, the runtimes that record against it are not.

chainCount.description: Chains the recorder would enumerate, capped at depth 4. The unit the recording actually costs; machine count is not, since a 70-machine domain yields 104 chains and a 71-machine one yields 277.

status.description: recorded — a shard exists and the corpus it names is the corpus as it stands. stale — the corpus moved; see drift. unrecorded — no shard, a named gap rather than an absence. undatable — a shard predating corpus fingerprints, which cannot be shown to be current and is not recorded as though it were.

version.description: Content-addressed: the shard's contract version plus the first twelve hex of the corpus digest it was recorded against, e.g. 2.0.0+corpus.79f4300a2a5b. No counter is carried across builds, so the registry stays a pure function of its inputs and a changed version names the input that moved. null when unrecorded.

expectedVersion.description: The version a re-recording against today's corpus would carry. Equal to version exactly when the scope is current.

unresolvedSelectionEntries.description: Entries a corpus list names that resolve to no file under any root. Carried rather than dropped: a selection naming a machine that no longer exists is a finding about the selection.

drift.description: Present when stale. Three lists rather than a boolean, because 'stale' is the conclusion and 'which machines' is the finding.

quorum.description: 3-of-3 across cpp, LSP and Scala. Never a majority: a two-runtime agreement is a contract with an unexamined third.

counts.description: agreed / disagreement / noRuntimeEmits / unmeasurable. All four are carried: a chain no runtime emits for and a chain no runtime could be driven through are different facts, and neither is agreement.

chainCountAcrossScopes.description: Summed across scopes, which overlap: every corpus selection's machines also belong to a domain. Not a count of distinct chains.
